rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic usage associates al-ilāha with the sun, yielding a reading about leaving the sun to be worshipped.
rows.anchor: يعني الشمس , فيكون تأويل الآية : ويذرك والشمس حتى تعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turned from killing Moses to killing Israelite sons because he thought Moses was beyond his reach, through strength or divine protection.
rows.anchor: إما لقوته وإما تصوره أنه مصروف عن قتله

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: One gloss takes Pharaoh's threat to inspect the women's wombs, deriving the verb from a term for the private part.
rows.anchor: مأخوذ من الحياء وهو اسم من أسماء الفرج , حكاه ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent meaning is that Pharaoh would keep the women alive because they were too weak to resist or fight.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الأظهر أن معناه : نستبقيهن أحياء لضعفهن عن المنازعة وعجزهن عن المحاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses may have urged reliance on God to console them under Pharaoh's threat.
rows.anchor: أنه أمرهم بذلك تسلية لهم من وعيد فرعون كما يقول من نالته شدة : استعنت بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he promised that God would help them against Pharaoh if they sought His help.
rows.anchor: أنه موعد منه بأن الله سيعينهم على فرعون إن استعانوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience may mean enduring their hardship in hope of God's reward.
rows.anchor: واصبروا على ما أنتم فيه من الشدة طمعا في ثواب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses ordered patience while they awaited God's victory.
rows.anchor: أنه أمرهم بالصبر انتظارا لنصر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of the earth consoles them: worldly rule does not last for Pharaoh, since lands pass between peoples.
rows.anchor: أن الدنيا لا تبقي على أحد فتبقي على فرعون لأنها تنتقل من قوم إلى قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses was signaling that God would give them Pharaoh's land.
rows.anchor: أنه أشعرهم بذلك أن الله يورثهم أرض فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous end may mean reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يريد في الآخرة بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean victory in this world.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا بالنصر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One account says the Israelites were harmed both before and after Moses came by being charged the poll tax.
rows.anchor: أن الأذى من قبل ومن بعد أخذ الجزية . قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: جويبر
rows.claim: Earlier they labored half a day and used the rest to earn their own food; afterward they were made to work all day without food or drink.
rows.anchor: تسخيرهم بني إسرائيل في أعمالهم لنصف النهار وإرسالهم في بقيته ليكسبوا لأنفسهم . والأذى من بعد : تسخيرهم في جميع النهار بلا طعام ولا شراب , قاله جويبر

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Another account identifies earlier harm as enslavement and killing sons, and later harm as a threat to renew that treatment.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أن الأذى الذي كان من قبل : الاستعباد وقتل الأبناء , والذي كان من بعد : الوعيد بتجديد ذلك عليهم , حكاه ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Earlier they made bricks while being given straw; afterward they still made bricks but had to supply the straw themselves.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا يضربون اللبن ويعطيهم التبن , والأذى من بعد أن صاروا يضربون اللبن ويجعل عليهم التبن , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The phrase may mean before Moses brought the prophetic message and after he brought it.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن تأتينا بالرسالة ومن بعد ما جئتنا بها , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the promise from God that Moses would deliver them, both before and after he brought that promise.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن تأتينا بعهد الله إليك أنه يخلصنا ومن بعد ما جئتنا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their complaint may have been a plea for help against what Pharaoh had done to them.
rows.anchor: أنه شكوى ما أصابهم من فرعون واستعانة بموسى

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Alternatively, they said it because they were impatient for Moses' promise to be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: أنهم قالوه استبطاء لوعد موسى , حكاه ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, عسى expresses hope and apprehension.
rows.anchor: { عسى } في اللغة طمع وإشفاق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God says عسى, its fulfillment is certain.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن عسى من الله واجبة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise interprets عسى from God as certainty.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : { عسى } من الله يقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb فَيَنْظُر may mean that God will see how they act.
rows.anchor: { فينظر } وجهان : أحدهما : فيرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean that God will know how they act.
rows.anchor: والثاني : فيعلم وفي قول موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' statement both promises victory and succession in the land and warns them against corruption there.
rows.anchor: الوعد بالنصر والاستخلاف في الأرض . والثاني : التحذير من الفساد فيها لأن الله تعالى ينظر كيف يعملون

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Asaf can mean regret over what has passed.
rows.anchor: أنه المتأسف على فوت ما سلف قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses asaf as grief.
rows.anchor: أنه الحزين , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses asaf as intense anger.
rows.anchor: هو الشديد الغضب , قاله الأخفش

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses asaf as being incensed.
rows.anchor: والرابع : المغتاظ , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses asaf as remorse.
rows.anchor: والخامس : النادم , قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that Moses was angry with his people for worshipping the calf and grieved over missing his communion with God.
rows.anchor: غضبان من قومه على عبادة العجل ؟ أسفا على ما فاته من مناجاة ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses was angry with himself for leaving his people, and grieved at their sins after he saw them.
rows.anchor: غضبان على نفسه في ترك قومه حتى ضلوا , أسفا على ما رأى في قومه من ارتكاب المعاصي

rows.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
rows.claim: Some Sufis say he was angry at leaving communion with the Real to address created beings.
rows.anchor: إن غضبه للرجوع عن مناجاة الحق إلى مخاطبة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says they were a bad replacement because they worshipped the calf after him.
rows.anchor: يعني بعباة العجل

rows.speaker: الحسن والسدي
rows.claim: They explain the hastening as abandoning Moses' promised forty nights because the people thought he had died when he missed the thirtieth night.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه قدروا أنه قد مات لما لم يأت على رأس الثلاثين ليلة , قاله الحسن , والسدي

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: A later view says they hastened God's promise of reward for worship by turning to worship another instead.
rows.anchor: وعد ربكم بالثواب على عبادته حتى عدلتم إلى عبادة غيره , قاله بعض المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajala means doing something before its time, while surʿa means doing it in less time.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين العجلة والسرعة أن العجلة : التقدم بالشيء قبل وقته , والسرعة : عمله في أقل أوقاته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses threw the tablets in anger when he saw the people worshipping the calf.
rows.anchor: غضبا حين رأى عبادة العجل , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Moses saw the virtues of Muhammad's community, asked that they be his community, and threw the tablets in anguish when told they were Ahmad's community.
rows.anchor: قال : تلك أمة أحمد , فاشتد عليه فألقاها , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah had seven parts; six were lifted after the tablets broke, leaving guidance and mercy in the remaining seventh.
rows.anchor: وكانت التوراة سبعة أسباع فلما ألقى موسى الألواح فتكسرت رفع منها ستة أسباعها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the tablets broke and all but one sixth was taken up.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : ألقى موسى الألواح فتكسرت ورفعت إلا سدسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about taking Aaron by the head has two readings: Moses took his ear, or his whole head.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أخذ بأذنه . والثاني : أخذ بجملة رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that custom changes whether such an act counts as humiliating, and it may not have been humiliating then.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الفعل مما قد يتغير حكمه بالعادة فيجوز أن يكون في ذلك الزمان بخلاف ما هو عليه الآن من الهوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer compares Moses' action to someone now taking hold of his beard or biting his lip.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك منه كقبض الرجل منا الآن على لحيته وعضه على شفته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Moses called Aaron son of his mother because Aaron was his maternal brother.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان أخاه لأمه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this is an Arab expression appealing to kinship to soften the listener.
rows.anchor: على عادة العرب استعطافا بالرحم , كما قال الشاعر :

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic address, son of my mother and twin of my soul, illustrates the appeal to kinship in Aarons plea.
rows.anchor: يا ابن أمي ويا شقيق نفسي … أنت خليتني لأمر شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enemies are those who opposed Aaron over the calf worship; their opposition made them his enemies.
rows.anchor: يعني من خالفه في عبادة العجل لأنهم قد صاروا لمخالفتهم له أعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to be angry with him as with the wrongdoers, since he was not one of them; this softened Moses.
rows.anchor: أي لا تغضب علي كغضبك عليهم ولست منهم فأدركته الرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance from sins means regretting past wrongdoing and resolving not to repeat it.
rows.anchor: الندم على ما سلف والعزم على ألا يفعل مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of then believed is that they repented from sin and resumed the practice of faith afterward.
rows.anchor: يعني أنهم تابوا من المعصية واستأنفوا عمل الإيمان بعد التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they repented after sin and believed through that repentance.
rows.anchor: يعني أنهم تابوا بعد المعصية وآمنوا بتلك التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that they believed God accepts repentance.
rows.anchor: وآمنوا بأن الله قابل التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits “from,” and means Moses chose seventy men from his people.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام محذوف وتقديره : واختار موسى من قومه سبعين رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointment may be the earlier time associated with the request to see God.
rows.anchor: أنه الميقات المذكور في سؤال الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be a different appointment for repentance from worship of the calf.
rows.anchor: أنه ميقات غير الأول وهو ميقات التوبة من عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the seizure as an earthquake.
rows.anchor: أنها الزلزلة , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the seizure was death: the men died and were then brought back to life.
rows.anchor: أنه الموت . قال مجاهد : ماتوا ثم أحياهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says it was a fire that burned them; Moses thought they had died, though they had not.
rows.anchor: أنها نار أحرقتهم فظن موسى أنهم قد هلكوا ولم يهلكوا , قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the men were seized because they asked to see God.
rows.anchor: لأنهم سألوا الرؤية , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were seized because they had not forbidden worship of the calf.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لم ينهوا عن عبادة العجل قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may express fear that God included Moses and his people in a collective punishment, as warned at 8:25.
rows.anchor: سؤال استفهام خوفا من أن يكون الله قد عمهم بانتقامه كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it denies that they should be punished for the fools' deeds, since only wrongdoers are punished.
rows.anchor: أنه سؤال نفي , وتقديره : إنك ل تعذب إلا مذبنا فكيف تهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the seventy died as a trial rather than final death, distinguishing obedient people from sinners; Moses swooned, then God revived the dead.
rows.anchor: لا موت فناء ولكن موت ابتلاء ليثبت به من أطاع وينتقم به ممن عصى وأخذت موسى غشية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the fitna as punishment.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالفتنة العذاب , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fitna means trial and testing.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بها الابتلاء والاختبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested worldly good may mean blessing, so called because it feels good to people.
rows.anchor: أنها النعمة سميت حسنة لحسن موقعها في النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean good reputation and praise.
rows.anchor: أنها الثناء الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is the rewards due for obedience.
rows.anchor: أنها مستحقات الطاعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة وإبراهيم
rows.claim: These authorities gloss hudnā as repenting to God.
rows.anchor: معناه تبنا إليك , قاله ابن عباس , وسعيد بن جبير , ومجاهد , وقتادة , وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa says it means returning to God in repentance, from hāda-yahūdu, “to return.”
rows.anchor: رجعنا بالتوبة إليك , لأنه من هاد يهود إذا رجع , قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets it as drawing near to God through repentance, comparing it with a word for a means of closeness.
rows.anchor: يعني تقربنا بالتوبة إليك من قولهم : ما له عند فلان هوادة , أي ليس له عنده سبب يقربه منه , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may inflict punishment on whomever He wills among creation, as with Moses' people.
rows.anchor: من أشاء من خلقي كما أصيب به قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause concerns whom God wills to punish sooner or later.
rows.anchor: من أشاء في التعجيل والتأخير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Though universal in wording, mercy here specifically means mercy for believers from Muhammad's community, as the next clause specifies.
rows.anchor: أن مخرجها عام ومعناها خاص , تأويل ذلك : ورحمتي وسعت المؤمنين بي من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Mercy is universal in this world for righteous and wicked alike, but in the afterlife belongs only to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: أنها على العموم في الدنيا والخصوص في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the mercy is repentance, and applies it universally.
rows.anchor: أنها التوبة , وهي على العموم , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The God-fearing are those who avoid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: يتقون الشرك , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they are those who avoid sins.
rows.anchor: يتقون المعاصي , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zakat may mean the obligatory alms from their wealth, which is among the most demanding religious duties; this is the majority view.
rows.anchor: أنها زكاة أموالهم لأنها من أشق فرائضهم , وهذا قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan interpret zakat as obedience to God and His messenger: acts that purify the soul.
rows.anchor: معناه أي يطيعون الله ورسوله , قاله ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says the pronoun in “I shall write it” refers to prior blessings given to the Israelites: the earth as ritual purification and prayer space, with exceptions for impure or burial places.
rows.anchor: الأرض طهورا ومساجد يصلون فيها حيث أدركتهم الصلاة إلا عند مرحاض أو قبر أو حمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That account says God placed tranquility in their hearts and enabled them to recite the Torah from memory.
rows.anchor: وجعلت السكينة في قلوبهم , وجعلتهم يقرؤون التوراة عن ظهر ألسنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites asked to keep tranquility in a chest, read the Torah by looking at it, and pray only in the sanctuary; the account identifies the written mercy with these gifts.
rows.anchor: لا نستطيع حمل السكينة في قلوبنا فاجعلها لنا في تابوت , ولا نقرأ التوراة إلا نظرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report takes the written mercy to mean the previously mentioned tranquility, prayer, and recitation.
rows.anchor: يعني ما مضى من السكينة والصلاة والقراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One theory says God extracted the souls before bodies were created and gave them the knowledge needed to understand His address.
rows.anchor: أنه أخرج الأرواح قبل خلق الأجساد وجعل فيها من المعرفة ما علمت به من خاطبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that theory, some place the event in Paradise before Adam's descent to earth.
rows.anchor: أنه كان في الجنة قبل هبوطه إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others place it after Adam had descended to earth.
rows.anchor: أنه فعل ذلك بعد هبوطه إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second theory holds that God created souls and bodies together on earth.
rows.anchor: أنه خلق الأرواح والأجساد معا وذلك في الأرض

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say God stroked Adam's back between Mecca and Taif: white particles emerged on the right, the people of the right; black particles emerged on the left, the people of the left, and all testified before being returned.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل : وذلك أن الله مسح ظهر آدم بين مكة والطائف فخرج من صفحة ظهره اليمنى ذرية كالذر بيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God brought the offspring out generation after generation, age after age.
rows.anchor: أنه أخرج الذرية قرنا بعد قرن وعصرا بعد عصر

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians say God showed people their own selves and His power, thereby making them testify to His lordship.
rows.anchor: أنه دلهم على أنفسهم بما شهدوه من قدرته , قاله بعض المتكلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the testimony was their confession that God alone is Lord and one.
rows.anchor: هو إشهادهم على أنفسهم بما اعترفوا من ربوبيته ووحدانيته

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says the address was to Adam's fathers when their offspring were drawn from them, demonstrating that God created them after nonexistence.
rows.anchor: أنه قال ذلك للآباء من بني آدم حين أخرج من ظهورهم ذرياتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority say the address was to the offspring when God took them from their fathers' backs.
rows.anchor: أنه قال ذلك للذرية حين أخذهم من ظهور آبائهم , وهذا قول الأكثرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God addressed them through prophets after their reason had matured.
rows.anchor: أنه قال لهم : { ألست بربكم } على لسان الأنبياء بعد أن كملت عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God gave them reason by which they knew this and testified themselves.
rows.anchor: أنه جعل لهم عقولا علموا بها ذلك فشهدوا به على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhurriyya may derive from their emerging from the loins like tiny particles.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يخرجون من الأصلاب كالذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it derives from God bringing creation into being and making it manifest.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من ذرأ الله الخلق إذا أحدثهم وأظهرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created for Hell those who will end up there because of disbelief and sin.
rows.anchor: { ذرأنا لجهنم } أي خلقنا ممن يصير إلى جهنم بكفره ومعصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view restricts the many jinn and humans to children born of illicit unions, whose origins supposedly make them quicker to disbelief and sin.
rows.anchor: أراد أولاد الزنى لأنهم من النطف الخبيثة مخلوقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other view includes children of both lawful and unlawful unions, since people answer for their own actions, not their parents' deeds.
rows.anchor: أنه على العموم في أولاد الزنى والرشدة فيمن ولد من نكاح أو سفاح لأنهم مؤاخذون على أفعالهم لا على مواليدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts fail to understand the truth, their eyes fail to see guidance, and their ears fail to hear admonition; neglect makes them as if these senses were absent.
rows.anchor: فصاروا بترك استعمالها بمثابة من عدمها

rows.speaker: مسكين الدرامي
rows.claim: Al-Darimi's couplet about being blind when a neighbor leaves and deaf to what happened illustrates the failure to use the senses.
rows.anchor: أعمى إذا ما جارتي خرجت … حتى يواري جارتي الجدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says all God's names are beautiful.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كل أسمائه حسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning of the beautiful names is the names hearts prefer to invoke, such as mercy and forgiveness rather than anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: ما مالت إليه القلوب من ذكره بالعفو والرحمة دون السخط والنقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are the names God deserves for Himself and His acts, including His being first, everlasting, powerful, knowing, living, one, hearing, seeing, and self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: أسماؤه التي يستحقها لنفسه ولفعله ومنها صفات هي طريقة المعرفة به , وهي تسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God by the names may mean invoking Him in petition.
rows.anchor: نداؤه بها عند الرغبة إليه في الدعاء والطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean glorifying Him by worshipfully remembering these names.
rows.anchor: تعظيمه بها تعبدا له بذكرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets those who deviate regarding God's names as those who lie.
rows.anchor: معناه يكذبون , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets it as associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: يشركون , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses it as distorting or altering the names.
rows.anchor: يحورون , قاله الأخفش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: One explanation is that idol names were derived from God's names, such as al-Lat from Allah and al-Uzza from al-Aziz.
rows.anchor: اشتقاقهم آلهتهم من أسماء الله , كما سموا بعضها باللات اشتقاقا من الله , وبعضها بالعزى اشتقاقا من العزيز , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they named idols gods and called God the father of the Messiah and Ezra.
rows.anchor: تسميتهم الأوثان آلهة والله عز وجل أبا المسيح وعزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not withdraw victory over enemies until a people change their trust and reliance on Him.
rows.anchor: حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم من الثقة به والتوكل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading concerns the loss of protection from enemies when people abandon obedience and commit disobedience.
rows.anchor: حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم من طاعته والكف عن معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may withdraw wealth and abundance when people stop paying His due from it.
rows.anchor: حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم . من تأدية حق الله تعالى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that God's reward changes when people abandon faith.
rows.anchor: حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم من الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may withdraw guidance when people cease to submit to Him.
rows.anchor: حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم من الانقياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the fāʾ, “from yourselves” may mean from among the most obedient to God.
rows.anchor: من أكثركم طاعة لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same reading may mean from among you in the finest character.
rows.anchor: من أفضلكم خلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also mean from among you in the noblest lineage.
rows.anchor: من أشرفكم نسبا

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي
rows.claim: With ḍamma on the fāʾ, it may mean from the believers, untouched by any idolatry.
rows.anchor: يعني من المؤمنين لم يصبه شيء من شرك , قاله محمد بن علي

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad says it means born in lawful marriage, with no pre-Islamic illegitimate ancestry; a prophetic report says he came from marriage, not fornication.
rows.anchor: يعني من نكاح لم يصبه من ولادة الجاهلية , قاله جعفر بن محمد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says he came from lawful marriage and not fornication.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( خرجت من نكاح ولم أخرج من سفاح )

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it means from among people whom you know.
rows.anchor: ممن تعرفونه بينكم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it means from all the Arabs, since every Arab tribe had some relation of birth to him.
rows.anchor: يعني من جميع العرب لأنه لم يبق بطن من بطون العرب إلا قد ولدوه , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAzīz ʿalayhi mā ʿanittum means that your hardship is severe for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: شديد عليه ما شق عليكم , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن أبي عروبة
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Abi ʿAruba interprets it as your going astray being severe for him.
rows.anchor: شديد عليه ما ضللتم , قاله سعيد بن أبي عروبة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads the phrase as the hardship endured by the believers being severe for him.
rows.anchor: عزيز عليه عنت مؤمنكم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet is keen for you to believe.
rows.anchor: حريص عليكم أن تؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His compassion may be shown through the guidance he commands and the welfare he wants for people.
rows.anchor: بما يأمرهم به من الهداية ويؤثره لهم من الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is shown by removing burdens and pardoning people's slips.
rows.anchor: بما يضعه عنهم من المشاق ويعفو عنهم من الهفوات , وهو محتمل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: If they turn away, al-Hasan says they turn away from obedience to God.
rows.anchor: عن طاعة الله , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Alternatively, they turn away from the Prophet himself.
rows.anchor: عنك , ذكره علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God is sufficient for me” may mean sufficient as a helper against them.
rows.anchor: حسبي الله معينا عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is sufficient as a guide for them.
rows.anchor: حسبي الله هاديا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne may be described as great because of its vastness.
rows.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : لسعته . الثاني : لجلالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, its greatness denotes majesty.
rows.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : لسعته . الثاني : لجلالته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Yusuf ibn Mihran says these two verses were the last revealed from the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: روى يوسف بن مهران عن ابن عباس أن آخر ما أنزل من القرآن هاتان الآيتان

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says these verses were the most recent in their covenant with God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب : هما أحدث القرآن عهدا بالله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the two verses had been revealed earlier at Mecca, unlike the reports that they were the latest revelation.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : تقدم نزولهما بمكة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says God gives the believers a light by which they walk.
rows.anchor: يجعل لهم نورا يمشون به , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj's explanation is that their deeds guide them to Paradise.
rows.anchor: يجعل عملهم هاديا لهم إلى الجنة , وهذا معنى قول ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God guides them to the road to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن الله يهديهم إلى طريق الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may simply praise them by describing them as guided.
rows.anchor: أنه وصفهم بالهداية على طريق المدح لهم

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abu Malik says the rivers flow beneath the inhabitants' dwellings.
rows.anchor: من تحت منازلهم قاله أبو مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the rivers flow before them, visible from above; the verse about Egypt's rivers uses “beneath me” to mean before me.
rows.anchor: تجري بين أيديهم وهم يرونها من علو لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq says the rivers of Paradise flow without riverbeds, as transmitted by Abu ʿUbayda.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيدة عن مسروق أن أنهار الجنة تجري في غير أخدود

rows.speaker: الربيع وسفيان
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ and Sufyan say that when the people of Paradise desire something, they say “Glory be to You, O God,” and it comes to them.
rows.anchor: إذا اشتهوا الشيء أو أرادوا أن يدعوا بالشيء قالوا سبحانك اللهم فيأتيهم , ذلك الشيء , قاله الربيع وسفيان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says their tasbih is the form of supplication they use when they seek something from God.
rows.anchor: إذا أرادوا الرغبة إلى الله في دعاء يدعونه كان دعاؤهم له : سبحانك اللهم : قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes their greeting as safe dominion in Paradise, since taḥiyya can mean dominion; a poet uses the word this way.
rows.anchor: معناه وملكهم فيها سالم . والتحية الملك , ومنه قول زهير بن جنان الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the inhabitants greet one another with peace, safe from the trials suffered by the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: أن تحية بعضهم لبعض فيها سلام . أي : سلمت وأمنت مما بلي به أهل النار , قاله ابن جرير الطبري

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Their final supplication may be praise of God, just as their first was tasbih; this likely is Qatada's view.
rows.anchor: أن آخر دعائهم : الحمد لله رب العالمين , كما كان أول دعائهم : سبحانك اللهم , ويشبه أن يكون هذا قول قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, after receiving what they desired through tasbih, they thank God and praise Him.
rows.anchor: إذا أجابهم فيما دعوه وآتاهم ما اشتهوا حين طلبوه بالتسبيح قالوا بعده : شكرا لله والحمد لله رب العالمين
